- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.53) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.27) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the lower bound to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — adjust downward by 2–5% for days 1–7.  
- When sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative or vice versa), model often lags — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 3–7% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation — if sentiment is volatile, cap forecast variance at ±5% of recent 14-day range.
